components.name: agentic_pipeline
components.author: Dagster Community
components.description: Whole agentic pipeline in one YAML. `source: + steps: + outputs:` — every step becomes a first-class Dagster asset with cost / latency / tokens / router-reasoning as metadata. 16 ops for the common shapes (single call, routing, debate, critique, synthesis, MCP tool calls, tool-use loops, framework handoffs, map, extract, classify, reduce, self-reflect, sub-pipelines, calls to pre-built agents). Any LiteLLM provider. Reusable `personas:` + pre-built `agents:` declared once and referenced by name.

agent_hints.when_to_use: User wants a standardized multi-step agentic workflow shape declared in ONE YAML. v2 covers 6 ops: llm_call | route | debate | critique_loop | synthesize | mcp_call. Supports typed named `inputs:` on every text-emitting op — any op can join from any prior op by port name (execution-plan graph shape). Sibling of ml_pipeline / polars_pipeline / warehouse_pipeline for the LLM domain. NEW: `partition_key_parser:` lets a composite partition key (like `dagster-io/dagster#30000`) unpack into `{partition.owner}` / `{partition.repo}` / `{partition.issue_number}` placeholders reachable in every string field (tool_args, prompt_template, system_prompt, source.text, sink paths). Pair with `PartitionedAssetLauncherJobComponent` for the config-driven-partition pattern. Also supports `tool_use_loop` op — open-ended agent loop with MCP tools, LangGraph-style, bounded by max_iterations, materialized as ONE Dagster asset with the full tool-call trajectory in metadata. NEW: `handoff` op composes with existing framework runtimes (LangGraph / AutoGen / CrewAI / DSPy) — user's callable becomes ONE step of the Dagster pipeline; adjacent steps stay Dagster-native. Framework's per-node lineage is inside that asset's metadata, not the Dagster graph.
agent_hints.typical_upstream: Literal text prompt, a fetched URL / doc, a file, another Dagster asset (via upstream_asset source), or a direct MCP tool call (via mcp_call op — no upstream needed).
agent_hints.typical_downstream: Text sinks (files), JSON sinks (full step dicts w/ per-op metadata), or downstream Dagster assets that consume any of the emitted step-output asset keys — every step is a first-class asset.
example_prompts: Build an agentic pipeline that routes an incoming ticket to the right specialist agent, then critiques and refines the answer, then synthesizes a final response.
Standardized multi-agent workflow with router + debate + critique loop — all in one YAML.
Multi-step LLM pipeline where a cheap router picks a specialist, then multiple proposers debate the answer, then an arbitrator picks the winner.

AI maintainer investigation room: fetch a GitHub issue via GitHub MCP, fan out 4 typed-input specialists (repo/docs/repro/history), synthesize a triage decision, skeptic critique, decision routing, final report — all one YAML using mcp_call + typed inputs.
Investment memo generator: 3 analyst proposers debate buy/hold/sell for a ticker, arbitrator picks the winner.

MIR triage pipeline where a launcher job takes issue_number + owner + repo via run config, derives a composite dynamic partition key, and the pipeline uses {partition.owner}/{partition.repo}/{partition.issue_number} in mcp_call tool_args.
agent_hints.side_effects: Calls LLM providers (OpenAI / Anthropic / etc. via LiteLLM). Optionally writes text/JSON sinks to disk. Emits multiple named asset outputs from one component. mcp_call op invokes external MCP servers (stdio subprocess / http / sse).

llm_call_with_typed_inputs.system_prompt: Join the two contexts and apply the policy.

tool_use_loop.system_prompt: You are a research agent. Use the tools to gather information, then call `finalize` with your answer.

agent_hints.anti_uses: Fields: `asset_name_prefix` (NOT `asset_name`). **`source:` is for INITIAL TEXT INPUT ONLY** — its shape is one of {kind: literal, text: '...'} | {kind: file, path: '...'} | {kind: url, url: '...'} | {kind: upstream_asset, upstream_asset_key: '...'}. **NEVER put a step (mcp_call, llm_call, etc.) inside `source:`**. If your FIRST step is an `mcp_call` or otherwise doesn't need upstream text, put it as `steps[0]` and set `source: {kind: literal, text: 'unused'}`. Each step has {id, op, ...op-specific args}. For joins use `inputs: {port_name: {from: step_id} | {literal: value}}` — each port becomes a `{port_name}` placeholder in prompt_template + system_prompt (and, for mcp_call, in string tool_args). mcp_call op fields: `server: {name, type: stdio|http|sse, command|url}`, `mcp_tool_name`, `tool_args: {key: value}` (static dict, NOT LLM-generated). `outputs.assets` MUST list ALL step ids you want as first-class Dagster assets. mcp_call `server.command` for stdio MUST be a LIST of strings [executable, ...args] — NOT a single space-separated string. Passing a string produces cryptic `FileNotFoundError: 'n'` at runtime (Python splits it per character).

steps_schemas.description: Per-op discriminated union for entries in `steps:`. Validate each step against the schema matching its `op:` field.

source.description: Optional prior step id; defaults to most recent.

command.description: stdio transport: LIST of strings — [executable, ...args]. MUST be a list, NOT a bare space-separated string. e.g. [npx, -y, "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"].

mcp_tool_name.description: Name of the tool as the MCP server exposes it (get_issue, read_file, etc.).

tool_args.description: Static keys; string values support {text} and {port_name} substitution.

source.description: Optional prior step id; defaults to most recent. Text goes into `prompt_template` as `{text}`.

inputs.description: Typed named inputs (port substitution in system_prompt / prompt_template).

model.description: LLM the agent runs on. Should be a strong model (gpt-4o, claude-3-5-sonnet) — the agent has to plan.

system_prompt.description: Agent instructions. Default guides toward calling the synthetic `finalize` tool when done.

max_tokens.description: Max tokens per LLM call (not per loop).

items.description: Same shape as mcp_call.server — stdio | http | sse | fastmcp.

mcp_servers.description: MCP servers whose tools the agent has access to. list_tools() is called on each at loop start to build the tool catalog.

allowed_tools.description: Optional allowlist of tool names. Defaults to ALL tools from ALL configured servers.

finalize_tool_name.description: Name of the synthetic finalize tool the LLM calls to end the loop with a final answer. Default 'finalize'.

source.description: Optional prior step id; defaults to most recent.

entry_module.description: Python module path with the user's callable.

initial_state.description: Kwargs passed to the callable. String values get {text} + {port_name} substitution.

output_text_key.description: Key in returned dict whose value is downstream text. Default 'final_answer'.

framework.description: Metadata-only label (langgraph|autogen|crewai|dspy|...); surfaces in asset metadata.

source.description: Optional upstream ref. Its text becomes {extra.src_text} for a card's tool_args_template/HTTP payload -- NOT automatically part of task.

inputs.description: Typed named ports ({port: {from: step_id}}) substituted as {port_name} directly into task before anything else happens.

task.description: Free-text description of what this step needs done; also passed to the invoked agent as its instruction.

required_tags.description: Pre-filter candidate agent cards by skill tag before the picker LLM sees them.

required_capabilities.description: Pre-filter candidate agent cards by capabilities (our own verb taxonomy -- critique/supervise/triage/translate/... -- NOT part of A2A or MCP) before the picker LLM sees them.

input_mode.description: MIME type of what this step is sending (default text/plain). Candidates that declare default_input_modes but don't list this are dropped; cards without declared modes are never excluded on this basis.

validate_mcp_schema.description: Default true. For an MCP-backed pick, validates the rendered tool_args against the picked agent's real, server-declared inputSchema before calling.

registry.description: Discovery config: sibling AgentCardComponent instances (discover_siblings, default true) + an optional external agent-card manifest (manifest_url/manifest_path, same dual-source loader as CatalogAgentComponent).

fallback.description: agent_id to use if the picker fails to pick validly.

source.description: Optional prior step id; defaults to most recent. Its text is parsed as a JSON list and converted to a DataFrame for the target component's input.

component_type.description: Dotted path, e.g. 'dagster_community_components.FilterComponent'. Any existing component with a real compute function.

attributes.description: Dict passed to the target component's constructor -- same shape as its own YAML attributes: block. Asset-graph-specific fields the target's own schema requires (asset_name, upstream_asset_key/source) still need SOME value to satisfy that component's validation, even though this op bypasses the graph entirely.

input_kwarg.description: Which of the target asset's input names receives this step's data. Auto-detected when the target declares exactly one input; required if it declares more than one.

asset_name.description: If the target's build_defs() returns more than one asset, which one (by Dagster asset name) to invoke.

resources.description: Forwarded to dagster.build_asset_context(resources=...), for a target that needs a real Dagster resource to run.

emitted_assets.pattern: One Dagster asset per step listed in `outputs.assets`. Asset key = `{asset_name_prefix}_{asset_id}`.

components.name: Aggregate Freshness Sensor
components.description: Alert when an entire selection of assets has gone silent, as one signal instead of hundreds of per-asset alerts. Polls the most recent materialization (or observation) across a whole selection. alert_mode picks how that gets reported: 'check' (default) emits an AssetCheckEvaluation against a declared rollup asset, alertable via Dagster+'s Asset alert type; 'fail_tick' raises on the sensor itself (no asset created), alertable via Dagster+'s Automation alert type targeting this exact sensor by name. Distinct from post_processing's per-asset attributes.freshness_policy, which answers 'is this one asset stale' rather than 'did the whole feed stop'.
components.author: Dagster Community

validation.notes: Built and tested (13 passing tests). Added alert_mode after confirming via real Dagster+ alert-policy docs that 'Asset' alerts scope by asset key/selection/group (not a specific check name) while 'Automation' alerts CAN target one named sensor directly -- but only fire on sensor TICK failure, which this component's check-based design deliberately never does. fail_tick mode trades the check/tick-failure distinction away for precise sensor-level alert targeting and zero synthetic assets. Verified raising inside a @dg.sensor function is caught and recorded as a tick failure by Dagster's sensor daemon. Also added monitored_folder after confirming one defs.yaml CAN hold multiple ---separated component documents (verified in Dagster's own source: parse_yamls_with_source_position), but that this component specifically can't be co-located that way with its parent dagster.DefsFolderComponent -- confirmed a real RecursionError from context.build_defs() re-entering the currently-resolving document, not fixable via any monitored_folder value.

agent_hints.when_to_use: Alert when an entire group of assets has gone silent (e.g. a replication feed with hundreds of tables on mixed cadences going fully dark) -- not when one asset individually misses its own SLA. Pair with a Dagster+ 'asset check failed' alert policy on the declared rollup_asset_key.
example_prompts: Alert us if NOTHING in this whole SnowPipe feed has loaded in 10 minutes, without firing a separate alert for every individual table.

components.name: argo_workflow_sensor
components.description:
Fire a Dagster job when an Argo Workflow reaches a terminal success phase.

Two modes — set exactly one of ``workflow_name`` or
``workflow_template_label``:

  - ``workflow_name`` — watch one specific Workflow by name. Useful
    when Dagster knows the workflow's name (e.g. it triggered it).

  - ``workflow_template_label`` — list workflows by a label selector
    like ``workflows.argoproj.io/workflow-template=nightly-agg``
    and watch the most-recently-completed one. Useful when Argo's
    scheduler creates workflows on its own cadence and Dagster
    wants to react to the latest finish.

Example:
    ```yaml
    type: dagster_community_components.ArgoWorkflowSensorComponent
    attributes:
      sensor_name: argo_nightly_done
      workflow_template_label: workflows.argoproj.io/workflow-template=nightly-aggregation
      namespace: argo
      host_env_var: ARGO_SERVER_URL
      token_env_var: ARGO_TOKEN
      job_name: downstream_processing_job
      asset_key: argo/etl/nightly_aggregation
    ```
components.author: Dagster Community

validation.evidence: build_defs + Pydantic instantiation pass; awaiting customer pilot for live

agent_hints.outputs: Polls Argo Server REST API for workflow status; emits AssetMaterialization / AssetObservation + RunRequest on terminal success.

components.name: argo_workflow_trigger
components.description:
Trigger an Argo Workflow run via the Argo Server REST API.

Example — submit from a WorkflowTemplate with parameters:

    ```yaml
    type: dagster_community_components.ArgoWorkflowTriggerComponent
    attributes:
      asset_key: argo/etl/nightly_aggregation
      workflow_template: nightly-aggregation
      namespace: argo
      parameters:
        INPUT_DATE: "2026-05-27"
        REGION: us-east-1
      host_env_var: ARGO_SERVER_URL
      token_env_var: ARGO_TOKEN
    ```

The returned workflow name (Argo generates it server-side, often
with a 5-char suffix like `nightly-aggregation-xyz12`) lands in
asset metadata so a paired ``argo_workflow_sensor`` can pick it up.

**Do NOT pair on the same asset_key as ``external_argo_workflow``** —
those represent the same workflow with different schedule ownership.
Pick the Case (A or B) that matches your setup; the components are
alternatives, not complements.
components.author: Dagster Community

validation.evidence: build_defs + Pydantic instantiation pass; awaiting customer pilot for live

components.name: Budget Asset
components.description: Per-asset $ cost tracking with rolling window budget enforcement. Cost estimated via `cost_per_second` (wall-clock rate) or `cost_fn` (`mod:fn` callable given (context, elapsed_s, result) → USD). Cumulative cost history read from ASSET_OBSERVATION event log (`budget_cost_estimate_usd` metadata within `window_days`). Enforcement modes: warn (observation), fail (dg.Failure pre-flight or post-flight), skip (return MaterializeResult(budget_skipped=true) pre-flight). Companion @budget decorator.
components.author: Dagster Community

validation.evidence: Live-validated via dagster.materialize on persistent DagsterInstance: warn+cost_per_second emits cost=$0.10 for 0.1s@$1/s; cost_fn(tokens*$0.000002) emits $0.01 for 5000 tokens; on_breach=fail rejects both post-flight (cost > budget) and pre-flight (cumulative ≥ budget); on_breach=skip runs once, second run skipped with budget_skipped=true observation.

validation.evidence: Live-verified, nothing mocked: full python-mode pipeline (chunk -> classify -> embed -> write_vector_store) against real sentence-transformers embeddings, real HuggingFace zero-shot classification, and a real ChromaDB write, including a real semantic search query correctly retrieving the matching chunk with citation metadata; source: {kind: warehouse_query} against a real DuckDB database via dagster-duckdb (this caught and fixed a real bug: DuckDBResource.get_connection() is a @contextmanager -- calling it without `with` raises AttributeError, confirmed live); max_source_rows truncation reporting both counts in metadata; all mutual-exclusivity/execution_mode/sql_dialect/output_table validation guards. Mocked (no free/local backend exists): embed provider='litellm' and classify mode='llm' -- litellm's own call is mocked, request/response handling runs for real. Structural only, not executed (no live warehouse credentials in this environment): execution_mode='sql' -- the generated SQL is asserted for all 3 dialects (snowflake_cortex, bigquery, databricks) but never run against a real warehouse.

components.name: Data Contract
components.description: Enforce a data contract at materialization — schema (per-column types/nullability/uniqueness/range/enum/regex), freshness SLA (max lag from prior materialization via event log), row-count SLA (drop% vs prior via event log). Emits one AssetCheckResult per contract rule + AssetObservation tagged with contract_version + owners + consumers. Contract version drives `code_version` on the asset so downstream can automatically invalidate on version bumps. Two shapes: this YAML component defines a new asset; the `@data_contract` decorator wraps an existing @dg.asset. on_violation=block raises dg.Failure (asset does not materialize); on_violation=warn materializes anyway, downstream blocks via AutomationCondition.
components.author: Dagster Community

validation.evidence: Both shapes live-validated via `dagster.materialize` with a persistent DagsterInstance: (1) PASS path — 3-row DataFrame, 3 schema checks (int unique + float min>=0 + string in allowed_values), all AssetCheckResults passed, asset materialized. (2) VIOLATION path — same schema, DataFrame with duplicate order_id + negative amount + bad currency → 3 AssetCheckResults ERROR-severity with typed descriptions ('1 duplicate(s) in unique column', 'min=-5.0 < required 0', 'values not in allowed set: [XYZ]'), dg.Failure raised, asset did NOT materialize.

agent_hints.inputs: Optional upstream_asset_key. Compute is user-provided Python (returns pandas DataFrame).
agent_hints.outputs: One @dg.asset with N AssetCheckSpecs (one per contract rule). code_version=contract.version so downstream detects version bumps. AssetObservation tags: contract_version, contract_owners, contract_consumers.
agent_hints.side_effects: Emits AssetCheckResult per rule (schema/freshness/sla), AssetObservation with contract metadata. Reads prior materializations from context.instance.get_event_records for SLA + freshness comparison.

components.name: db2_resource
components.author: Dagster Community
components.description:
Register an IBM Db2 resource for use by other components.

Pairs with the generic SQL components — ``dataframe_to_table``,
``sql_command_job``, ``warehouse_maintenance_job``, ``database_replication``,
``database_schema_inventory`` — by exporting its SQLAlchemy URL.

Example (Docker Db2 Community Edition — Linux/Unix/Windows):

    ```yaml
    type: dagster_community_components.Db2ResourceComponent
    attributes:
      resource_key: db2_resource
      host: localhost
      port: 50000
      database: testdb
      username: db2inst1
      password_env_var: DB2_PASSWORD
      system_type: luw                  # default — can omit
    ```

Example (Db2 on Cloud):

    ```yaml
    type: dagster_community_components.Db2ResourceComponent
    attributes:
      resource_key: db2_resource
      host: '<id>.databases.appdomain.cloud'
      port: 31198
      database: bludb
      username: bluadmin
      password_env_var: DB2_CLOUD_PASSWORD
      ssl: true
      system_type: cloud
    ```

Example (Db2 for i / AS/400 / iSeries):

    ```yaml
    type: dagster_community_components.Db2ResourceComponent
    attributes:
      resource_key: db2_iseries_resource
      host: as400.example.com
      # port defaults to 446 when system_type=iseries — DRDA listener
      database: 'S101ABCD'              # *LOCAL system name (RDB) — see your IBM i
      username: QSECOFR
      password_env_var: AS400_PASSWORD
      ssl: true                         # almost always required on i 7.x+
      system_type: iseries
      library_list:                     # AS/400 search path
        - MYAPP
        - MYAPP_DATA
        - QSYS2
    ```

    Notes for AS/400:
      - ``host`` is the IBM i system hostname or IP.
      - ``database`` is the **Relational Database Directory (RDB) name**
        (often the *LOCAL system name). Find it with
        ``WRKRDBDIRE`` on the i — the entry marked ``*LOCAL``.
      - ``library_list`` maps to ``CURRENT SCHEMA`` (first entry) +
        ``CURRENT PATH`` (rest). Schema-inventory and migration
        components honor this when ``database_type='db2_iseries'``.
      - The catalog lives at ``QSYS2.SYSTABLES`` / ``QSYS2.SYSCOLUMNS``,
        NOT ``SYSCAT.*``. Use ``database_schema_inventory`` with
        ``database_type: db2_iseries`` for AS/400-aware queries.

agent_hints.outputs: IBM Db2 Dagster resource — connection string + connection factory shared across assets.

agent_hints.when_to_use: User wants a single YAML surface to wire event triggers (run failures / durations / stuck / slow startup, asset materializations / observations / check failures, metric thresholds / metadata matches / value changes, freshness violations / absences, log-pattern matches on events + stdout + stderr, daemon or Dagster+ agent heartbeat failures, code location load errors, backfill status transitions, sensor failure meta-observability, concurrency-hit guardrails, step-level errors, SQS messages) to actions (materialize / launch_job / webhook / slack / pagerduty / discord / email / teams / opsgenie / mattermost / sns / sqs / cancel_run / retry_run / toggle_sensor / toggle_schedule). Compound AND/OR supported with one level of nesting. Prefect-Automations analog for Dagster covering all Dagster+ platform events (Serverless + Hybrid K8s/ECS/Docker agents).
agent_hints.typical_upstream: Any Dagster job or asset that emits run-status events / materializations. External HTTP endpoints (for http_poll). AWS SQS queues (for sqs_poll). agent_hints.typical_downstream: Alerting channels: Slack / PagerDuty / Discord / Teams / OpsGenie / Mattermost / email. AWS SNS + SQS for cross-service event fanout. components.name: Lifecycle WAP
components.description: Write-Audit-Publish (WAP) lifecycle for assets. Wraps a compute function; writes output to a STAGING location; runs audit checks; on ALL pass promotes staging → prod, on any fail applies quarantine/discard/tag_and_keep policy. Each audit check emits an AssetCheckResult visible in Dagster's asset-check panel — downstream can block via AutomationCondition. Three backends in v1: filesystem (parquet/csv/json, local + fsspec URIs), SQL (via sqlalchemy, transactional table swap), Iceberg (via pyiceberg, branch fast_forward). Companion `@lifecycle` decorator wraps existing @dg.asset functions.
components.author: Dagster Community

validation.evidence: Both shapes live-validated end-to-end via `dagster.materialize` on fresh uvx project: (1) pass path — 6-row DataFrame + row_count_min=5 passed → PUBLISHED, prod file exists, staging removed, AssetCheckResult passed. (2) fail path — 3-row DataFrame + row_count_min=100 failed → QUARANTINED (file at .quarantine/daily_fail.parquet.<ts>), prod not created, AssetCheckResult ERROR severity.

agent_hints.inputs: Optional upstream_asset_key. Compute function is user-provided Python (returns pandas DataFrame).
agent_hints.outputs: One @dg.asset emitting a DataFrame + N AssetCheckResults (one per audit rule). Materialization metadata: wap_write_kind, wap_all_passed, wap_publish_outcome, wap_row_count, wap_check_summary, backend-specific paths.
agent_hints.side_effects: Writes to staging location (file / table / branch), runs audits, then either promotes to prod OR quarantines/discards. Never publishes bad data.
agent_hints.anti_uses: Not for streaming assets (single DataFrame return only). Not for TB-scale in-memory (uses pandas). Not a replacement for full data-quality frameworks (Great Expectations, Soda) — the python audit-check kind can delegate to those.
requires_resources: conditionally: sql resource_key if write.kind=sql and using a Dagster resource

components.name: ml_pipeline
components.author: Dagster Community
components.description: Standardized end-to-end ML pipeline in one YAML — source + steps + outputs. 36 ops covering feature engineering, hyperparameter tuning (grid / random / **bayesian** via Optuna), evaluation, interpretability, and model persistence. Any sklearn / XGBoost / LightGBM estimator via `sklearn_class:` escape hatch. Opt-in `experiment_tracking:` block auto-logs params / metrics / model artifacts to MLflow and/or Weights & Biases from every train / evaluate / *_search / cross_validate step. Rich per-step metadata (elapsed_seconds, model_class, hyperparams, CV mean/std, evaluate metrics, top feature) surfaces as `MetadataValue` on emitted assets — promote to Dagster+ Insights for training-cost / accuracy dashboards. Warehouse-connected via any Dagster resource. Partition-aware.

agent_hints.when_to_use: User wants a standardized ML pipeline shape (source → feature-eng → split → train → evaluate → sinks) declared in one YAML. Covers the 80% ML case (tabular data, sklearn/xgboost/lightgbm models). Sibling of polars_pipeline / warehouse_pipeline / pyspark_pipeline for the ML domain.
agent_hints.typical_upstream: A warehouse table (via warehouse_query source), a CSV URL / file, or another Dagster asset (via upstream_asset source).
agent_hints.typical_downstream: Warehouse tables (predictions, feature importance), CSVs / parquet files (side outputs), saved model artifacts (joblib), or downstream inference services.
example_prompts: Build an ML pipeline that trains a decision tree on my Snowflake customer_features table and writes predictions back.
Standardized ML pipeline with grid search + SHAP interpretability + saved model artifact — all in one YAML.
Wine ML pipeline: fetch UCI dataset, scale features, split, train, cross-validate, write CSVs.
agent_hints.side_effects: Writes to disk (csv/parquet/joblib sinks) or a warehouse (table_sinks via Dagster resources). Emits multiple named asset outputs from one component.

validation.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eric-thomas-dagster/dagster-community-components-cli/main/examples/wine_ml_pipeline_component.md . Follow-up code audit (added 2026-09-28): this component had exactly ONE test before this date, covering only the warehouse_query/table_sink path -- not one of the 36 ops was exercised. A full code-reading audit (not doc-driven) of every op found and fixed 3 real bugs, now covered by 8 new committed tests: (1) the shipped quick example (README.md) and example.yaml both fed predict/evaluate the pre-split 'scaled' frame instead of 'split' (the step that actually carries the split column), and evaluate/confusion_matrix/predict never auto-filter by split -- meaning the shipped examples' own accuracy numbers were computed partly or fully on rows the model was fit on; fixed both examples and added a documented 'Avoiding train/test leakage' pattern (filter to split=='test' between predict and evaluate). (2) can_subset's dependency-closure computation only covered _FRAME_OPS despite its own comment claiming _FRAME_OPS + _MODEL_TRAIN_OPS coverage -- a sourceless train/grid_search/random_search/bayesian_search step (the shape both shipped examples use) got zero recorded dependency, so a partial materialization could silently train on the raw unsplit/unscaled frame instead of the intended one; fixed. (3) register_model's sample-frame lookup for Snowflake Registry schema inference grabbed whatever frame ran most recently in the pipeline instead of the frame that actually trained the model being registered (e.g. a train -> predict -> importance -> register_model pipeline would wrongly grab importance's feature/importance columns); fixed via a new __model_source_frame__ tracking dict. Also fixed: grid_search/random_search/bayesian_search's best CV score was computed and logged to console only, never reaching Dagster metadata or the experiment tracker (contradicted this component's own docs); experiment_tracking.mlflow.log_params/log_metrics were documented as opt-out toggles but never actually checked; log_artifacts was documented as a real option with zero implementation anywhere (now a real mlflow.log_table call, gated behind the flag, default off). Also removed an unused `requests` dependency (the url/file ingestion path uses pd.read_csv via fsspec, never requests).

emitted_assets.pattern: One Dagster asset per step listed in `outputs.assets`. Asset key = `{asset_name_prefix}_{asset_id}`.

components.name: Partition Lock Asset
components.description: Cross-run partition-scoped mutex via Dagster event log. Scans recent ASSET_OBSERVATION events for partition_lock_acquired=<partition_key> newer than ttl_seconds; conflicts resolve per on_conflict (wait/skip/fail). Emits partition_lock_acquired on entry + partition_lock_released post-compute. TTL auto-expires stuck holders. Probabilistic — two runs within ~200ms could both acquire; adequate for backfill dedupe, not money transfers. Companion @partition_lock decorator.
components.author: Dagster Community

validation.evidence: Live-validated via dagster.materialize on persistent DagsterInstance: fresh acquire+release; second run acquires again after release; planted conflicting lock → on_conflict=skip returns MaterializeResult(partition_lock_skipped=true); on_conflict=fail raises dg.Failure; TTL expiry — 1s ttl + 1.5s wait → lock treated as stale, acquire succeeds.

components.name: RAG Grounding Check
components.description: Verify RAG-generated answers are actually grounded in their retrieved source chunks -- rag_eval's sibling for generation faithfulness rather than retrieval quality. Deterministic n-gram overlap + fabricated-number detection by default (free, no API key), with an opt-in mode='llm_judge' for nuanced cases. Attached asset check fails on regression vs the prior materialization, mirroring rag_eval.
components.author: Dagster Community

validation.evidence: Live-verified, nothing mocked: mode='overlap' scoring on genuinely-grounded and genuinely-ungrounded (fabricated-detail) answers, including a regression test for a real false positive found live ('Q3' misread as the number '3' before a word-boundary fix); cross-materialization regression detection (mirrors rag_eval exactly) -- a first 'good' materialization passes, a second 'bad' one correctly detects the drop and fails; source: {kind: warehouse_query} against a real DuckDB database; max_fabrication_rate/mutual-exclusivity/invalid-mode validation guards. Mocked (no free/local backend exists): mode='llm_judge' -- litellm.completion is mocked, prompt construction/JSON parsing/score-mapping logic verified for real.

agent_hints.inputs: Query/answer/sources rows via upstream_asset_key (e.g. rag_pipeline's generate-step output) or source: {kind: warehouse_query, resource_key, sql}.
agent_hints.outputs: Upstream rows with grounding_score, grounded, fabricated_numbers (and judge_reasoning for mode='llm_judge') columns added, plus mean_grounding_score/fabrication_rate metadata.
agent_hints.side_effects: None on data -- attaches an asset_check that fails on quality regression, an absolute floor, or excess fabrication rate.
agent_hints.anti_uses: For retrieval quality (did we fetch the right chunks), use rag_eval instead; this one only checks whether an already-generated answer is supported by its already-retrieved sources.

components.name: rejection_feedback_loop
components.description: Sensor that watches an approval-token directory for `approved: false` tokens with a `feedback: "..."` field, and re-triggers an upstream job with that feedback captured as new input — letting the agent revise based on the human's specific rejection reason. Bounded by `max_iterations` so a stubborn agent can't loop forever. Composes with HumanApprovalGate / SlackApprovalGate / TeamsApprovalGate via shared `approval_dir`. Writes feedback to `{approval_dir}/.feedback/{partition_key}.txt` — pipeline reads it via a `synthesize` step (typed input `feedback: {from: <file-reader-step>}`) OR a plain `source: {kind: file, path: ...}`. Moves consumed rejection tokens to `.consumed/` so they aren't re-processed. Persists iteration state in `.state/{partition_key}.json`. Optional companion state DataFrame asset for observability into which partitions are mid-loop.
components.author: Dagster Community

components.description: Cross-run concurrency limit keyed on a named pool. components.name: Smart Retry
components.description: Retry classification beyond Dagster's built-in RetryPolicy — retry on HTTP 429 + 5xx but fail immediately on 400/401/403/404. Classifies raised exceptions against configurable rules (HTTP status codes, exception classes) and re-raises as Dagster RetryRequested (retryable) or Failure (permanent). Wraps a Python callable, shell command, or one-off HTTP call. Configurable backoff + jitter + max attempts.
components.author: Dagster Community

validation.evidence: Full end-to-end: (1) classifier 7/7 unit-tested; (2) transient retry-then-succeed via Python callable; (3) permanent fail-fast via ValueError; (4) rate_limit fail mode (3 calls capped); (5) circuit_breaker cross-materialization (r1 opens, r2 fails without touching compute); (6) LIVE LLM classification via real gpt-4o-mini calls — TimeoutError → transient, ValueError missing-field → permanent.

agent_hints.inputs: Optional upstream_asset_key. Compute callable receives context (+ upstream value if wired).
agent_hints.outputs: One asset with materialization metadata: attempts (int), compute_kind. On failure adds classification / exception_class / http_status.
agent_hints.side_effects: Whatever the wrapped compute does (network / shell / DB). Retries + backoff SLEEP block the step in-process — cheaper than Dagster step-level RetryPolicy which re-launches the whole step.
agent_hints.anti_uses: Not for compute that has no exception-based failure mode. Not for step-level worker-death retries (use Dagster RetryPolicy for that — they compose). Not for very slow compute where in-process sleep would timeout the step.

validation.evidence: Verified end-to-end against a real local Dagster materialization for BOTH input modes: upstream_asset_key (file_lister -> this component) and path (this component listing files directly, no separate asset) -- litellm.completion mocked to avoid real API spend. Preset resolution, the custom-with-no-output_fields error path, the unknown-document_type error path, and the both-modes/neither-mode-set error path all behave as documented. Also verified post_process (move and delete): successfully-extracted rows' source files are moved/deleted, a failed row's file is left in place for retry, and both post_process='move' without post_process_dir and post_process set with input_type='text' raise the documented validation errors. Also verified against REAL files: a real PNG is base64-encoded correctly into a vision content block (decoded bytes checked against the real PNG header, not just mocked), a real digitally-generated PDF has its actual pdfplumber-extracted text reach the prompt instead of raw PDF bytes, a PDF with no extractable text fails that row cleanly (previously this whole file-reading path silently produced garbage for every PDF/image -- opened in text mode with errors='replace' regardless of extension), llm_max_retries is forwarded to litellm's num_retries, and malformed/non-object LLM JSON responses are handled as clean per-row failures. Also verified field_regions: a region crop was checked pixel-by-pixel (a red/blue split test image) to confirm the correct area is cropped and sent as an extra labeled content block alongside the full image; no field_regions set produces exactly the prior message shape.

components.name: teams_approval_gate
components.description: Microsoft Teams HITL approval gate. Slack analog — same asset + sensor shape, same JSON token format, composes with HumanApprovalGateComponent via shared `approval_dir`. Uses MS Graph API (Azure AD app registration with application permissions ChannelMessage.Read.All + ChannelMessage.Send + admin consent). Two approval modes: `reactions` (default; approvers react with a built-in Teams emoji — like/heart/laugh/surprised/sad/angry, limited to 6) OR `reply` (approvers post a thread reply containing a configured keyword like APPROVE/REJECT — more flexible, allows context in the same message). Multi-approver quorum + allowlist + timeout policies (escalate / reject / approve). Sensor polls Teams API every `poll_interval_seconds` and writes the standard JSON approval token on quorum. Works without a public webhook (unlike Teams Adaptive Card interactive buttons) — deployable to Dagster+ Serverless with no infra changes.

components.name: Video Scene Summarizer
components.description: Detect scene changes in a video via ffmpeg and summarize each one with a vision-LLM call -- a table of contents for video, one row per scene (timestamp, frame, summary).
components.author: Dagster Community

validation.evidence: Verified end-to-end against REAL ffmpeg-generated videos (not just mocked content, litellm.completion mocked to avoid real API spend): a real 3-scene video (red->blue->green hard cuts) correctly detects 2 scene boundaries at the right timestamps, extracts real non-empty frame files, and each scene gets a (mocked) LLM summary; a genuinely static video correctly falls back to a single first-frame row instead of producing zero rows; a corrupt/unreadable video is counted as a real error in video_errors output metadata instead of failing the whole run or being silently skipped. Two real ffmpeg compatibility bugs were caught and fixed by this real-file testing (not visible against mocks): -vsync vfr was removed in ffmpeg 9.x (now -fps_mode vfr), and ffmpeg exits nonzero -- not zero -- when the scene filter matches no frames at all (handled explicitly rather than treated as a hard failure).

agent_hints.inputs: A DataFrame with a column of video file paths (e.g. file_lister's local_path column, or synthetic_video_generator's file_path column).
agent_hints.outputs: New DataFrame, one row per detected scene: video_id, source_video, scene_index, timestamp_seconds, frame_path, summary.
agent_hints.side_effects: Shells out to ffmpeg for scene detection + frame extraction; calls a vision-LLM provider (OpenAI/Anthropic/etc via LiteLLM) once per detected scene.
agent_hints.anti_uses: For a fixed-cadence frame dump (every N seconds/frames) with no LLM call, use video_frame_extract_asset instead. For audio-only transcription, use audio_transcriber/speech_to_text_asset.

components.name: Warm Scheduled Job
components.description: Isolated, always-warm job that manages one or more cron schedules in-process, bypassing Dagster's SchedulerDaemon entirely (its minute-granular tick evaluation is architectural, not a load artifact -- confirmed against the Dagster OSS scheduler source, which Dagster+'s control plane subclasses unchanged). Warms up once per bounded run (load a model, open connections), then fires each job's tick_fn as a direct in-process function call at each precise scheduled instant -- never through Dagster's run-launching APIs, which is what makes each tick instant and keeps the process genuinely isolated (dedicated resources, not the shared code-location server). Supports a single job (flat asset_name/schedule/tick_fn fields) or several independently-scheduled jobs sharing ONE warm process and ONE warmup pass (the `jobs` list) -- each job still gets its own AssetKey/materialization history. By default, each job's real cadence is also documented as a default-STOPPED, non-firing Dagster ScheduleDefinition (targeting a harmless no-op marker asset, never the real automation) so it's visible in the Schedules tab. Pair with StreamingRunHealthSensorComponent, unmodified, for auto-restart.

validation.evidence: Live-verified (real croniter, real wall-clock sleeps, nothing mocked): warmup runs exactly once per bounded run and every tick observes the identical warm_state object; measured drift against the scheduled instant is sub-500ms; tick_error_handling='continue' survives a failing tick and keeps looping ('raise' correctly fails the whole run); max_seconds and max_ticks both correctly bound the loop; a malformed cron string, a 6-field string without second_precision=true (croniter's own is_valid() is too lenient to catch this alone -- confirmed live it accepts 6-field and even 7-field strings regardless of the second_at_beginning flag, so this component enforces its own strict field-count check first), an invalid dotted callable path, and an invalid timezone are all rejected with clear errors at build_defs time. Not yet verified: multi-hour DST transitions in non-UTC timezones, or behavior under catchup=true with a very large missed-tick backlog beyond max_catchup_ticks.

components.name: Zuora Account Upsert
components.description: Reverse-ETL sink: mirror an upstream DataFrame into Zuora Account records via the generic Object CRUD API. Zuora has no upsert-by-key endpoint and no filter-by-field GET -- this component queries by lookup_field first via ZOQL (POST /v1/action/query) to discover an existing Account Id, then issues PUT /v1/object/account/{id} (update) or POST /v1/object/account (create). Two API calls per row. Create requires Name, Currency, BillCycleDay, and Status in fields_map -- no defaults are supplied.
